paragraphs.source_en: Tiger, tiger, crimson as if set aflame, in the thicket at midnight, what godlike vast eye or hand could sketch your terrifying majesty? At what far-away abyss of the sea, or out on the sky’s highest edge, is the pure crystal that burns with your eye-fire? With what wings does it dare to rise and fly? By what hand dares it to seize that terrifying, towering might? What kind of shoulders and wrists—what kind of divine power— can carve into the system of your entrails? When your heart has just begun to beat alive, what shocking hands, what shocking feet are those? What hammer is pounding it? What forge is being used? In what great furnace is your brain-essence being simmered? What is the anvil block? What monstrous grip dares to seize such ferocious terror and dread? When the stars cast their golden rays, and the whole sky overflows with their tear-bright gleam, seeing its workmanship, does he show a smile? Is it not the divine craft that made the lambs that pursues you? Tiger, tiger, crimson as if in flame, in the dark-night thicket, what godlike giant eye or hand dares to sketch your frightening grandeur?
